theme: Immigrate — UK Route, Visit & Visitor Visas

topics.label: Visitor Visa (TRV) — standalone page
topics.metaDescription: Temporary Resident Visa (TRV) requirements: ties assessment, funds, and common refusal reasons. Free application review from a licensed RCIC.
topics.lead: A Temporary Resident Visa (TRV) is required for citizens of many countries to enter Canada as a visitor. Officers assess each application primarily on whether the traveller is likely to leave Canada by the end of their authorized stay.

topics.label: eTA (Electronic Travel Authorization)
topics.metaDescription: eTA requirements for visa-exempt travellers flying to Canada: eligibility, validity period, and how it differs from a visitor visa.
topics.lead: An eTA is a lightweight entry requirement for citizens of visa-exempt countries arriving in Canada by air — electronically linked to the traveller's passport rather than issued as a physical visa document.

topics.label: Super Visa — standalone page
topics.seoTitle: Super Visa Canada 2026: Parents & Grandparents | CMG
topics.metaDescription: Super Visa requirements: invitation letter, sponsor income, and mandatory medical insurance for parents and grandparents visiting Canada.
topics.lead: The Super Visa is a long-validity, multiple-entry visa for parents and grandparents of Canadian citizens or permanent residents, allowing stays of up to 5 years per visit without the annual renewals a standard visitor visa would require.

topics.label: Business Visa
topics.metaDescription: Business visitor rules for Canada: what activities qualify without a work permit, and how this differs from an employer-specific work permit.
topics.lead: Business visitor status covers temporary entry for those attending meetings, conferences, or exploring business opportunities in Canada, without entering the Canadian labour market — meaning no separate work permit is required.
headings: What Qualifies as a Business Visitor

topics.label: Transit Visa
topics.seoTitle: Canada Transit Visa 2026: Airport Connections | CMG
topics.metaDescription: Transit visa and Transit Without a Visa (TWOV) requirements for travellers connecting through a Canadian airport en route elsewhere.
topics.lead: A transit visa may be required for travellers passing through a Canadian airport on their way to another country, without formally entering Canada — whether a visa or the visa-free transit program applies depends on nationality and connecting flight details.

topics.label: Visitor Record
topics.seoTitle: Visitor Record Canada 2026: Extend Your Stay | CMG
topics.metaDescription: How to extend visitor status in Canada with a Visitor Record — application timing, implied status, and what it does and doesn't authorize.
topics.lead: A Visitor Record is the document confirming an extension of authorized visitor status in Canada, generally applied for from within the country before the original authorized stay expires.

topics.label: Canada Work Permit (overview)
topics.seoTitle: Canada Work Permit 2026: Types, LMIA & Requirements | CMG
topics.metaDescription: Employer-specific, LMIA-exempt, or open work permit — find the right route to work in Canada. Requirements, LMIA process, and timelines. Free RCIC review.
topics.lead: A Canadian work permit is either tied to a single employer or open to work for almost any employer — and that distinction determines which documents are required, how long processing takes, and how the permit connects to a future permanent residence application.

topics.label: Canada Study Permit
topics.seoTitle: Canada Study Permit 2026: DLI, PAL & PGWP Rules | CMG
topics.metaDescription: Study permit requirements for 2026: DLI selection, Provincial Attestation Letters, and how your program choice affects PGWP and PR eligibility.
topics.lead: A study permit application is strongest when it's planned around where it leads — a Post-Graduation Work Permit, then Canadian work experience, then a route to permanent residence — not evaluated purely on getting the permit approved in isolation.
headings: The Study Permit → PGWP → PR Route
